title: automat environment profile
description: An ENVIRONMENT profile: which control sets to compile, where the account lands, what behavior is permitted inside it, and what in-account baseline to deploy. Input to `automat vend` (DESIGN 7). Named 'environment' rather than 'profile' because automat has three unrelated document types that were all called profiles — this one, obligation profiles (which regime, assessed how), and classification profiles (which institutional data level) — and an evidence record naming 'profile id + content hash' was ambiguous to exactly the auditor it exists for. 'Environment' is also the idiom higher ed already uses for a resource rated to hold data at a level. Obligation and classification profiles are POLICY artifacts; the environment profile is the thing being BUILT.

review_by.description: The date by which this environment profile must be re-read against the posture it claims to deploy. REQUIRED, with no default. An environment profile names control sets, a placement, a permitted-behavior boundary, and a baseline; left alone it keeps vending the posture someone approved once, and every account it produces looks as current as the day it was written. `verify` warns once this date has passed. The field is inside the document, so it is covered by the content hash recorded in the evidence manifest and by any attestation over it — extending the date is a change no earlier attestation vouches for.

signatures.description: Optional attestations over this document's content hash (see $defs/attestation). PROVENANCE ONLY: an attestation says who stood behind this document in what capacity — typically a central IT office recording `adopted-by` on the environment profile it publishes for departments to vend against — and never that its contents are correct, applicable, or approved for a given use. Trust is an operator determination; automat ships no trust anchor, no default accepted identity, and no verification in v1.

control_sets.description: Control set ids to compile into the artifact for this vend. Compiled by union (DESIGN 9).

placement.description: Where the vended account lands. New accounts always materialize under the root and are then moved (DESIGN 3, fact 4).

target_ou.description: Destination OU id. The account is moved here after creation.

create_intermediate_ous.description: Create missing OUs on the path. Bounded by the five-level OU nesting limit (DESIGN 3, fact 10).

ou_path.description: OU names to ensure beneath target_ou, outermost first. At most five levels total under the root.

email_pattern.description: Email template; '{name}' is substituted with the account name. Each account needs a globally unique email (DESIGN 3, fact 11).

role_name.description: Name of the management-assumable role created in the child. Defaults to OrganizationAccountAccessRole (DESIGN 3, fact 6).

tags.description: Additional tags applied at creation. automat's own conventional tags (DESIGN 14) are always applied and may not be overridden here.

baseline.description: In-child work performed after assuming into the account (DESIGN 7, step 5).

delivery_bucket.description: S3 bucket for the delivery channel. Created in-account when absent.

regions.description: Region posture. enable/disable are opt-in regions managed via the Account Management API; the region allowlist is enforced separately by SCP.

automation_role.description: Least-privilege in-account role automat uses for future verify runs, and which baseline-protection SCPs exempt (DESIGN 10).

disable_org_access_role_after_vend.description: Whether to restrict further use of the management-assumable role once baselining completes (DESIGN 7, step 5).

attestations.description: Where procedural-control attestation stubs are written.

evidence.description: Where evidence manifests are stored. A local copy is always written (DESIGN 11).

prose.description: Single-line human text. Control characters are rejected because these strings are rendered into reports and tables, where a newline forges a row.

long_prose.description: Multi-line human text. Newlines and tabs are permitted; other control characters are not.

attestation.description: One attestation over this document's content hash: an identity, the CAPACITY it acted in, and the statement it makes. A SIGNATURE ATTESTS PROVENANCE ONLY. It never attests that the document is correct, that it applies to any particular institution, or that anyone approves of its use. The roles exist precisely so that 'X wrote this', 'Y adopted it for its own use', 'Z reviewed it' and 'the format validated' cannot collapse into a single checkmark — a reader who sees one green tick learns nothing, and would reasonably infer the strongest of the four. Whether any identity here is TRUSTED is an operator determination, made against a trust policy the operator maintains naming accepted identities per role. automat ships NO trust anchor and no default accepted identity, performs no verification in v1, and is not and must never become a registry or a standards owner.

role.description: The capacity the identity acted in, and the only thing an attestation asserts. `authored-by` — this identity wrote the document. `adopted-by` — this identity uses it, which says nothing about who wrote it. `reviewed-by` — this identity read it and stands behind having read it, not behind the contents. `interpreted-by` — this identity produced the document as its own reading of someone else's published policy, and the source institution has neither reviewed nor endorsed it. `format-validated-by` — this identity checked that the document satisfies the published schema, which is a statement about syntax and nothing else. No role means 'approved', 'certified', or 'compliant', and none may be added that does: the value of the vocabulary is that the weakest claim cannot be read as the strongest.

identity.description: Who attests, as they wish to be identified — an institution, an office, an email address, an OIDC subject. Free prose because the useful identity is an institutional one and the eventual mechanism binds it to an OIDC identity rather than to a name automat could constrain.

statement.description: REQUIRED, and the reason this is an attestation rather than a signature. The identity says in its own words what it is claiming, so a reader evaluates a sentence rather than a tick. A bare signature invites the reader to supply the claim themselves, and they supply the strongest one available. Hashed with the rest of the document, so a statement cannot be rewritten under material that still verifies.

content_sha256.description: The document content hash this attestation is over. Recorded inside the document, which the schema cannot check for self-consistency — a validator must recompute it. Present anyway, because an attestation whose subject is implicit is one that can be moved to a different document.

attested_at.description: When the attestation was made. Required for the same reason `citations[].effective_date` is: an undated claim cannot be checked for staleness, and this one ages against `review_by`.

signature.description: The cryptographic material, WHEN THERE IS ANY. Optional and deliberately subordinate to the fields above: the claim is the attestation and the bytes are evidence for it, never the other way round. An entry with no signature is still a recordable attestation — an institution asserting authorship of a file it publishes itself — while bytes with no role and no statement are not expressible at all. automat performs NO verification in v1: it does not load a trust policy, does not resolve a key, and does not treat the presence of this block as meaning anything.

format.description: `detached-ed25519` is a raw detached signature over `content_sha256`, verified against a public key the operator obtains out of band. `oidc-identity-bundle` is the intended v2 mechanism: a keyless signature bound to an OIDC identity, so an institution never has to run a key ceremony, distributed alongside the document over git or an OCI registry. Both are named now so that adopting the second is not a schema version event.

value.description: Base64-encoded signature bytes, or the base64 bundle for the keyless form.

key_id.description: Which key signed, for the detached form. Required there: a detached signature nobody can locate a key for is unverifiable, which is worse than absent because it looks verifiable.

identity_issuer.description: The OIDC issuer that authenticated `identity`, for the keyless form. Required there and FORBIDDEN on the detached form, because in the keyless model the issuer is the whole of what makes the identity mean anything: 'signed by security@example.edu' is a different claim depending on who vouched for that address.
